statement: You are given a binary tree. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.
An inorder traversal first traverses a node's left subtree in inorder, then visits the node itself, then traverses its right subtree in inorder.
Return the node values in the order an inorder traversal visits them.

examples.explanation: The root 1 has children 2 and 3; 2 has children 4 and 5; 3 has only a right child, 6. The left subtree gives 4, 2, 5; then comes the root 1; then the right subtree gives 3, 6 (3 has no left child, so it comes before 6).
40 is the left child of 20, which is the left child of 10, so the walk starts at 40 and works back up before moving to 30.
